text:
yuki: running `redwoodctl init demo --local` inside WSL2 (Ubuntu) and it hangs after printing a URL. It tries to open a browser but nothing happens on Windows side. Anyone seen WSL <-> Windows browser handoff fail?

mike: what does the CLI print exactly?

yuki: paste: 
```
> redwoodctl init demo --local
device code flow started, opening browser for authentication...
waiting for auth...
# no browser opens on Windows, visiting the printed URL manually doesn't accept the code (shows invalid origin)
```

aditya: hmm, WSL2 attempts to use the $BROWSER env and the distro's xdg-open which maps to `wslview` or `explorer.exe` shim. If the CLI writes a browser URL with a file:// or weird fragment the Windows browser may drop the device code due to origin mismatch. Are you using Edge with Profiles/IE mode?

yuki: I'm on Windows 11 with Edge. I noticed the printed URL includes a trailing newline and the CLI log says `open: explorer.exe \"http://redwood.auth/....\n\"` (looks like the wrapper added quotes and newline). When I copy-paste the URL into Edge it complains about origin and won't accept the code.

mike: that quoting/newline looks like a WSL helper bug. Which `xdg-open` or `wslview` version do you have? `which wslview && cat $(which wslview)` might show a shim that mangles args. Also check `echo $BROWSER` in WSL.

yuki: `which wslview` -> `/usr/bin/wslview` (from distro). `echo $BROWSER` empty. When I run `wslview 'https://redwood.auth/device?c=ABCD'` it opens Edge but the URL gets percent-encoded wrong (space inserted). If I run `explorer.exe \"https://redwood.auth/device?c=ABCD\"` it opens ok.

aditya: two quick workarounds: 1) set BROWSER to explorer.exe in your WSL session: `export BROWSER='explorer.exe'` then run `redwoodctl login` so it uses explorer directly. 2) use headless mode instead: `redwoodctl login --headless --token-file=~/.config/redwood/wsl.token` and open the URL on any machine manually.

mike: we'll also add a small CLI improvement: when running under WSL detect common `wslview/xdg-open` shims and prefer `explorer.exe` if available. Also trim quotes/newlines from the open command to avoid mangled args.

yuki: tried `export BROWSER=explorer.exe` and `redwoodctl login --profile=wsl-test` — explorer opened and auth worked. Headless also works but less convenient. Thanks.

aditya: filed DX-6011: "redwoodctl: improve WSL browser handoff (prefer explorer.exe, strip quotes/newlines) and document BROWSER=explorer.exe workaround". Also adding a note in quickstart about WSL `wslview` shims and headless fallback.

cli-bot: Created ticket DX-6011: "redwoodctl: improve WSL browser handoff (prefer explorer.exe, strip quotes/newlines) and document BROWSER=explorer.exe workaround"

devex-bot: Added quickstart note: "If using WSL, set BROWSER=explorer.exe or use --headless to avoid browser shims interfering with SSO device flow." :white_check_mark:

yuki: leaving this thread so others in WSL don't get stuck. saved me 30m.
